title: Čech complex and cohomology commute with the first finite covering limit
statement:
Let $X$ be affine, $\Lambda$ a finite discrete ring, $F$ an étale sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules, and $M=\nu_X^*F$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $\mathcal V=\{V_a\to U\}_{a=1}^m$ be a nonempty finite basis covering and choose the first-limit systems $\mathcal V_j$ and $T_{\alpha,j}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-intersection-limit-compatibility]. The canonical restriction maps give an isomorphism of cochain complexes of abelian groups
$$\varinjlim_j\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V_j,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V,M),$$
and induce isomorphisms $\varinjlim_j\check H^q(\mathcal V_j,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\check H^q(\mathcal V,M)$ for every $q\ge0$. The complexes are the ordered alternating Čech complexes of [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech], including repeated indices. No injectivity of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the systems of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-intersection-limit-compatibility]. Their index set $J=\prod_{a=1}^m J_a$ is small, nonempty and directed: choose one coordinate in each $J_a$, and take coordinatewise upper bounds for two elements. For every ordered tuple $\alpha=(a_0,\ldots,a_p)$, that node supplies affine ind-étale $X$-objects $T_{\alpha,j}$ and $T_\alpha$, an identification $T_\alpha=\varprojlim_jT_{\alpha,j}$ with affine transitions, and compatibility of its projections with deleting any factor. Thus these are filtered colimits in the opposite affine ind-étale category to which section continuity applies. In particular the first-limit stages need not be étale over $X$.

Let $G$ be the underlying étale sheaf of sets of $F$. By [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the underlying set sheaf of $M$ is $\nu_X^*G$, with its addition obtained from that of $F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-classical-continuity-sets] to each diagram from step 1, including its merely ind-étale stages. This gives a bijection $\varinjlim_j |M(T_{\alpha,j})|\to |M(T_\alpha)|$ with legs the actual restriction maps. These restrictions are homomorphisms. The element and equality criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], with $R=\mathbf Z$, identifies the underlying set of the abelian-group colimit with this set colimit: both have stage representatives modulo eventual equality. Consequently the canonical homomorphism $c_\alpha:\varinjlim_j M(T_{\alpha,j})\xrightarrow{\sim}M(T_\alpha)$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Its value on a representative is $c_\alpha([j,s])=M(\pi_{\alpha,j})(s)$, where $\pi_{\alpha,j}:T_\alpha\to T_{\alpha,j}$.

Put $C_j^\bullet=\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V_j,M)$ and $C^\bullet=\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V,M)$. By [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech], their degree-$p$ terms are the products of the section groups indexed by $A_p=\{1,\ldots,m\}^{p+1}$. This set is finite for every fixed $p$, including tuples with repetitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] to its finite discrete indexing category. Composing its finite-product comparison with the $c_\alpha$ of step 2 gives an isomorphism $\phi^p:\varinjlim_j C_j^p\xrightarrow{\sim}C^p$. Explicitly $\phi^p([j,(s_\alpha)_\alpha])=(M(\pi_{\alpha,j})(s_\alpha))_\alpha$. This only interchanges a filtered colimit with one finite product at a time; it does not interchange a colimit with a product over all degrees.

Check the differentials on each colimit leg. For an ordered tuple $\beta$ of length $p+2$, let $\partial_r\beta$ delete its $r$-th entry, and denote the corresponding projections by $d_r:T_\beta\to T_{\partial_r\beta}$ and $d_{r,j}:T_{\beta,j}\to T_{\partial_r\beta,j}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-intersection-limit-compatibility], $\pi_{\partial_r\beta,j}\circ d_r=d_{r,j}\circ\pi_{\beta,j}$. Contravariant functoriality therefore gives $M(d_r)M(\pi_{\partial_r\beta,j})=M(\pi_{\beta,j})M(d_{r,j})$. For $s\in C_j^p$, the $\beta$ coordinate of restricting $\delta_j^p(s)$ is consequently $\sum_{r=0}^{p+1}(-1)^r M(d_r)M(\pi_{\partial_r\beta,j})(s_{\partial_r\beta})$, which is the $\beta$ coordinate of $\delta^p$ applied to the restricted $s$, by [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech]. The same identity holds for every transition $j\le k$ by the commuting product projections and functoriality. Hence the $C_j^\bullet$ form a diagram of complexes and the restriction maps to $C^\bullet$ form a cocone of complexes.

Form $L^p=\varinjlim_j C_j^p$ in every degree, with zero terms in negative degrees, and define its differential by $d_L^p\iota_j^p=\iota_j^{p+1}\delta_j^p$. The transition compatibility in step 4 makes this well-defined. Its square is zero because its composite with every $\iota_j^p$ is zero. This is the colimit complex: a cocone to any complex $K^\bullet$ induces unique maps $L^p\to K^p$, and these commute with differentials after precomposition with every colimit leg, hence commute outright. Step 4 also proves $\delta^p\phi^p=\phi^{p+1}d_L^p$. Thus the isomorphisms of step 3 assemble to a cochain map $\phi:L^\bullet\to C^\bullet$. Its degreewise inverses commute with differentials by multiplying this equation on both sides by the inverses. They give its inverse as a map of complexes. This proves the asserted canonical isomorphism of complexes.

By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], colimits over the small filtered category $J$ are exact in abelian groups. Apply [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] with $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Ab}$ and the nonnegative cochain shape. For every $q\ge0$ it identifies $\varinjlim_j H^q(C_j^\bullet)$ with $H^q(L^\bullet)$, with legs obtained by applying homology to the complex colimit legs. Compose with $H^q(\phi)$ from step 5. By [def-weil-pbc-cover-cech] this is exactly $\varinjlim_j\check H^q(\mathcal V_j,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\check H^q(\mathcal V,M)$. Its leg at $j$ is induced by the original restriction map $C_j^\bullet\to C^\bullet$, so the comparison is the one in the statement. At $q=0$ the incoming differential is zero, as specified in that definition. No injectivity, acyclicity, or vanishing has entered the argument.

No new nodes and no statement change.

The section-continuity input is lem-weil-pbc-proetale-classical-continuity-sets, which explicitly allows merely ind-étale stages. That is the right node, because the stages T_{α,j} are only étale over U, and U is only ind-étale over X. Step 1: the intersection-limit node supplies small directed J, ordered tuples with repetitions, affine ind-étale T_α and T_{α,j}, and face-compatible limits; the scheme limit inside B_X is a filtered colimit in the opposite category. Step 2: by the site-comparison definition, |ν^*F| is ν^*G; with the set continuity bijection and the elementwise module-colimit criterion (R=ℤ), the canonical map is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Step 3: the 002W node (abelian-group clause) commutes the colimit with one finite product per degree. Steps 4–5: the face equation π∘d_r = d_{r,j}∘π comes from the intersection node, and the colimit complex and its inverse are built correctly. Step 6: 00DB exactness plus the homology-preserves-exact-colimits node, with q=0 consistent (im δ^{-1}=0). Small cases checked: m=1, singleton J, empty intersections, F=0, noncommutative Λ. No duplicate: the second-limit stage-comparison node and the stage-3/cbc Čech-system nodes state different things. No SGA source, and no repair or re-split note exists for this item.
